source.citation: Wrede, H., Wagner, A. R., Pałubicki, W., Michels, D. L., Pirk, S. (2026). Flamescapes: Simulating the Wildlandfire Urban Interface. ACM Transactions on Graphics 45(6), Article 246.
source.licence: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), as stated on the paper's first page. © 2026 the authors.
source.changes: Equations retyped in LaTeX from page renders of the authors' PDF (project page https://helgewrede.github.io/flamescapes/, retrieved 2026-11-05); meanings, notes and symbol glosses are ours. Transcription errors are ours; cite the original.

conventions.ids: F1 to F19 are the main paper's numbered equations (1) to (19); S1 is the supplement's only numbered equation (1). Neither document has unnumbered display equations. Inline definitions (I1 to I4, S-I1, S-I2) and the mathematical lines of the algorithms (A1-2 from main Algorithm 1; S-A2-n from supplement Algorithm 2, line n) are listed separately under supplementary_expressions.
conventions.page: Page numbers are PDF pages, equal to article pages 246:n. Entries without a 'document' field belong to the main paper; supplement entries carry "document": "supplement" and supplement page numbers.
conventions.latex: LaTeX reproduces the printed equation, including suspected typos (see transcriber_note fields and the 'Transcriber's notes' sections of the two Markdown files).
conventions.symbols: Units in square brackets come from the paper's A.4 symbol list (main p. 19) where given; otherwise the gloss says 'unit implied' or 'not given'.
conventions.depends_on: Ids of equations whose quantities the entry uses directly.
conventions.parameters: Every numeric constant stated in the paper and supplement. 'value' is machine-readable (ranges as [min, max], vectors as lists, null when the table shows a dash); 'printed' keeps the original formatting where it differs; 'origin' is the Table 5 classification (Physical, Numerical, Scene).

equations.section: 4.2.1 Transforming Scene Geometry into the Solid Fuel Grid
equations.meaning: Estimates the volume fraction of each material in a voxel as the total in-material ray length over N rays cast through the voxel, divided by the total length the rays travel across the voxel.

symbols.N: number of rays per voxel [-] (64 by default)
symbols.l_{i,r}: accumulated length of ray r inside material i [m] (unit implied; foliage hits add an artificial length set by delta_l)
symbols.d_r: side length of the voxel crossed by ray r [m] (unit implied; equals the cell size Delta x)

equations.section: 4.2.1 Transforming Scene Geometry into the Solid Fuel Grid
equations.meaning: Adds a moisture volume fraction to the voxel in linear proportion to its dense (wood) and sparse (leaf) biomass volume fractions.

symbols.varphi_moisture: moisture volume fraction of the voxel [-]
symbols.varphi_dense: volume fraction of dense biomass, e.g. wood [-]
symbols.varphi_sparse: volume fraction of sparse biomass, e.g. leaves [-]
symbols.r_d: dense biomass moisture ratio [-] (value not given)
symbols.r_s: sparse biomass moisture ratio [-] (value not given)

equations.section: 4.2.1 Transforming Scene Geometry into the Solid Fuel Grid (Modeling of Interior Fuel)
equations.meaning: Total combustion energy available inside building b, computed as a sampled fire load density times the building floor area.

symbols.Q_b: total available combustion energy of building b [MJ] (unit implied by q''_b and A)
symbols.q''_b: total fire load density sampled for building b from the residential distribution of Dzolev et al. 2021 [MJ m^-2]

equations.section: 4.2.1 Transforming Scene Geometry into the Solid Fuel Grid (Modeling of Interior Fuel)
equations.meaning: Converts the building's interior fire load energy into an equivalent combustible solid mass using an effective net heat of combustion for mixed residential contents.

symbols.M_b: total initial combustible mass assigned to the interior of building b [kg] (unit implied)
symbols.Q_b: total available combustion energy of building b (Eq. 3)
symbols.Delta_c H^eff: effective net heat of combustion for mixed residential contents (value and unit not given)

equations.section: 4.2.1 Transforming Scene Geometry into the Solid Fuel Grid (Modeling of Interior Fuel)
equations.meaning: Draws the fuel mass of each interior solid voxel of building b from a normal distribution whose mean spreads M_b evenly over the interior voxels and whose spread follows the reported variability of residential fire loads.

symbols.m_{b,t}: fuel mass of interior voxel t of building b [kg per voxel]
symbols.mu_b: mean per-voxel fuel mass, mu_b = M_b / N_b [kg]
symbols.sigma_b: building-specific dispersion parameter derived from Dzolev et al. 2021 [kg] (value not given)
symbols.I_b: set of interior solid voxels of building b
symbols.N_b: number of interior solid voxels, N_b = |I_b| [-]

equations.meaning: Gas momentum equation without viscosity: the velocity changes under the pressure gradient and a buoyancy force that depends on how far the local gas density departs from the ambient reference density.
equations.transcriber_note: Sign of the buoyancy term depends on the unstated orientation of g; see Transcriber's note 9 in flamescapes-2026.md.

equations.meaning: Equation of state that sets the gas density from the gas temperature and the mixture's mean molar mass, so hot gas becomes lighter.

symbols.R: universal gas constant [8.314 J mol^-1 K^-1]
symbols.M_i: molar mass of species i [kg mol^-1]
symbols.n: index of the last species (number of species minus one)

equations.transcriber_note: Dimensionally the ideal-gas law needs a pressure where rho_amb stands; see Transcriber's note 8.

equations.meaning: Gas energy equation: gas temperature changes through heat conduction, a volumetric radiation term from soot, and heat released by gas-phase combustion (advection is handled separately in the semi-Lagrangian step).

symbols.C_{p,g}: specific heat capacity of the gas mixture [J kg^-1 K^-1]
symbols.nabla q_rad: volumetric radiation of the gas (Eq. 17); A.4 writes Delta q_rad [J s^-1]
symbols.qdot_{c,g}: combustion heat source in the gas phase (Eq. 9); A.4 unit for qdot_c [J s^-1]

equations.transcriber_note: Printed as a gradient of q_rad, not a divergence; A.4 units are per second, not per volume; sign of the radiation term conflicts with Eq. 17 (Transcriber's notes 2, 3, 7).

equations.meaning: Heat released by gas-phase combustion equals minus the (negative) heat of combustion times the molar combustion rate, kept unchanged from Fire-X.

symbols.qdot_{c,g}: gas-phase combustion heat source [J s^-1] (A.4; per unit volume in Eq. 8)
symbols.Delta_{c,g} H^0: heat of combustion of the gas fuel [J mol^-1] (Table 3: -8.34e5)

equations.meaning: Arrhenius-type global rate law for gas-phase combustion, depending on gas temperature and on the fuel and oxidizer molar concentrations raised to empirical exponents.

symbols.A_{c,g}: pre-exponential factor (units vary with reaction order; Table 3 gas Arrhenius factor 8.30e5 1/s)
symbols.E_{a,c,g}: activation energy for gaseous combustion [J mol^-1] (Table 3: 1.26e5)
symbols.R: universal gas constant [8.314 J mol^-1 K^-1]
symbols.T_g: gas temperature [K]; flame-front particles can supersede the cell temperature (Sec. 4.7)
symbols.c_0: molar concentration of oxidizer [mol m^-3] (printed c_0 in the equation, c_o in the text and A.4)
symbols.a: empirical reaction order exponent for fuel [-] (Table 3: -0.30)
symbols.b: empirical reaction order exponent for oxidizer [-] (Table 3: 1.30)

equations.meaning: Transport of each gas species mass fraction by advection and diffusion, with source terms from gas combustion and from the three new solid processes: moisture evaporation, pyrolysis and solid combustion.

symbols.D_i: diffusion coefficient of species i [m^2 s^-1]
symbols.mdot_{e,s}: solid evaporation source term [s^-1] (no equation given)

equations.meaning: Converts the molar gas combustion rate into a rate of change of each species mass fraction using its stoichiometric coefficient and molar mass.

symbols.mdot_{c,g}: gas combustion mass fraction source term [s^-1]
symbols.M_i: molar mass of species i [kg mol^-1]

equations.meaning: Mixing rules for a solid voxel: density is the volume-fraction-weighted sum of material densities, and specific heat (and, by the text, conductivity) is the volume-fraction-weighted mean of the material values.

symbols.rho_s: solid density of the voxel [kg m^-3]
symbols.C_{p,s}: specific heat capacity of the solid voxel [J kg^-1 K^-1]
symbols.C_{p,i}: specific heat capacity of material i [J kg^-1 K^-1] (Table 4)

equations.meaning: Pyrolysis of heated solid fuel where oxygen is lacking: the Arrhenius pyrolysis rate sets both the gaseous volatile source injected into the cell and the heat term in the solid energy equation.

symbols.M_i: molar mass of material i [kg mol^-1] (Table 4)
symbols.v_{p,s}: pyrolysis reaction rate, Arrhenius form analogous to Eq. 10 but not printed [kg m^-3 s^-1] (A.4); Table 3: activation energy 9.22e4 J/mol, Arrhenius factor 4.78e4 1/s
symbols.qdot_{p,s}: pyrolysis heat term in the solid energy equation [J s^-1] (A.4)
symbols.Delta_{p,s} H^0: heat of pyrolysis [J mol^-1 or J kg^-1] (Table 3: 2.50e05 J/kg)

equations.transcriber_note: Units of mdot_{p,s} and the sign of qdot_{p,s} conflict with A.4 and the text (Transcriber's notes 5 and 6).

equations.meaning: Oxidation of solid char or fuel when oxygen is present: the Arrhenius solid combustion rate sets the gaseous species source and the heat released in the solid.

symbols.mdot_{c,s}: solid combustion mass fraction source term [s^-1]
symbols.M_i: molar mass of material i [kg mol^-1]
symbols.v_{c,s}: solid combustion (oxidation) rate, Arrhenius form not printed [mol m^-3 s^-1] (A.4 unit for v_c); Table 3: activation energy 9.22e4 J/mol, Arrhenius factor 1.80e8 1/s
symbols.qdot_{c,s}: heat release by solid oxidation [J s^-1] (A.4)
symbols.Delta_{c,s} H^0: lower heat of combustion of the solid [J mol^-1] (Table 3: -2.80e6)

equations.transcriber_note: With the negative Table 3 value and no minus sign, qdot_{c,s} would be a sink (Transcriber's note 5).

equations.meaning: Net diffuse (Lambertian) radiative emission from a solid cell face adjacent to gas, relative to the ambient temperature; it is removed from the solid and carried by Monte Carlo rays to gas and other solids.

symbols.q_{rad,s}: radiative flux emitted by the solid surface [W m^-2] (unit implied)
symbols.epsilon: material emissivity [-] (no material values given; ember emissivity 0.95)

equations.meaning: Volumetric radiative emission of hot sooty gas, proportional to the soot mass fraction and an effective absorption coefficient, without wavelength dependence.

symbols.nabla q_rad: volumetric radiation of the gas [J s^-1] (A.4, written Delta q_rad)
symbols.kappa_s: effective absorption coefficient [-] per A.4 (dimensionally m^-1 in P_abs); Table 5 'Residual absorption coefficient' [500, 4000] may be this value (our reading)

equations.transcriber_note: Text calls this a loss term, but the printed sign makes it a gain when inserted in Eq. 8 (Transcriber's note 3).

equations.meaning: Solid energy equation: solid temperature changes by heat conduction through the voxelized solid plus the evaporation, oxidation and pyrolysis heat terms; radiative and ember deposits enter as additional sources in the implementation.

symbols.C_{p,s}: solid specific heat capacity [J kg^-1 K^-1] (Eq. 13)
symbols.k_s: solid thermal conductivity [W m^-1 K^-1] (mixing rule as for C_{p,s})
symbols.qdot_{c,s}: heat release by solid oxidation (Eq. 15) [J s^-1]

equations.meaning: Boundary condition at solid-gas interfaces (also applied inside porous cells): conductive flux out of the solid equals convective exchange with the neighbouring gas plus net surface radiation.

symbols.h: heat transfer coefficient, listed as dimensionless in A.4 (dimensionally W m^-2 K^-1); likely the Table 5 'Convection coefficient' [0, 200] (our reading)

equations.meaning: A wave function collapse building rule is a triple of scope, target condition and effect, where the effect keeps compatible states, removes incompatible ones, or changes state weights.

symbols.E: rule effect (keep, remove, or reweight states)

supplementary_expressions.section: 4.2.1 Transforming Scene Geometry into the Solid Fuel Grid (Modeling of Interior Fuel)
supplementary_expressions.meaning: Number of interior solid voxels of building b.

symbols.I_b: set of interior solid voxels of building b

supplementary_expressions.section: 4.2.1 Transforming Scene Geometry into the Solid Fuel Grid (Modeling of Interior Fuel)
supplementary_expressions.meaning: Mean of the per-voxel interior fuel mass distribution, fixed so that the expected total equals the fire-load mass M_b.

supplementary_expressions.section: 4.2.1 Transforming Scene Geometry into the Solid Fuel Grid (durability)
supplementary_expressions.meaning: Visibility test: a mesh module is removed from rendering once the combustible fuel mass left in its voxels falls below the fraction tau = 0.05 of its initial mass; it does not affect combustion.

symbols.D(t): current durability, sum of the module's remaining combustible fuel mass in voxels [kg]

supplementary_expressions.meaning: Probability that a radiation ray is absorbed by sooty gas over a path segment, used in the Monte Carlo ray transport; absorbed or solid-hitting rays deposit their energy and terminate.

symbols.kappa_s: effective absorption coefficient (A.4: dimensionless; dimensionally m^-1 here)

supplementary_expressions.meaning: Initial conditions of every grid cell: initial velocity, both temperatures at ambient (300 K with air at atmospheric pressure, Sec. 5.1) and initial species mass fractions.

symbols.Y_i^0: initial mass fraction of species i [-]

supplementary_expressions.transcriber_note: Sec. 5.1 calls the initial temperature T_0 (Transcriber's note 13).

supplementary_expressions.meaning: Each wall-cell semantic state exposes a discrete interface label on each of its four sides.

symbols.sigma: interface label function (not the Stefan-Boltzmann constant)

supplementary_expressions.meaning: Two neighbouring states are compatible in direction d exactly when their facing interface labels match.

symbols.d: direction from cell i to cell j

supplementary_expressions.meaning: Resets the per-cell accumulator of ember thermal energy.

symbols.qdot: ember thermal energy accumulated in the cell

supplementary_expressions.meaning: Excess thermal energy an ember brings into a solid cell: ember mass times its temperature excess over the solid times its heat capacity.

symbols.qdot_e: excess thermal energy of one ember (an energy despite the rate dot)
symbols.T_e: ember temperature [K] (not defined in the text)
symbols.C_e: ember heat capacity (not defined in the text)

supplementary_expressions.meaning: Sums the excess energy of all embers in the cell.
Raises the solid temperature by the deposited ember energy (printed as a multiplication by the volumetric heat capacity).

symbols.C_{p,s}: solid specific heat capacity [J kg^-1 K^-1]

supplementary_expressions.transcriber_note: Dimensionally a division by rho_s C_{p,s} (and cell volume) is expected; see supplement Transcriber's note 4.

supplementary_expressions.meaning: Resets the per-cell maximum flame-front particle temperature.

symbols.T_f: maximum flame-front temperature in the cell [K]

supplementary_expressions.meaning: Keeps the highest temperature carried by any flame-front particle in the cell.

symbols.T_p: temperature carried by a flame-front particle [K] (temperature of its originating cell)

supplementary_expressions.meaning: Temperature used in the gas combustion step: the larger of the flame-front temperature and the cell temperature, which lets ignition run ahead of the resolved burning region.
supplementary_expressions.transcriber_note: Main Sec. 4.7 and Eq. 10 suggest the gas temperature T_g; see supplement Transcriber's note 5.
